c8i.label: x86 (Intel Granite Rapids)
c8i.name: c8i.metal-48xl (Intel Granite Rapids)
c8i.about: AWS c8i.metal-48xl (bare metal; Intel Xeon 6975P-C, Granite Rapids, 96 cores), loaded speed at half load: one longest-first queue of the machine's timed jobs on every second physical core (against alone, ×1.00-1.07, procedure section 6)

c8g.label: Arm (Graviton 4)
c8g.name: c8g.metal-24xl (Graviton 4)
c8g.about: AWS c8g.metal-24xl (bare metal; Graviton 4, 96 cores), with the aarch64 builds, loaded speed at half load: one longest-first queue of the machine's timed jobs on every second physical core (against alone, ×1.01-1.23, procedure section 6)

notes: CBR only, strict buffer (bound 1.0), the first key frame's lookahead off. Builds from before --strict-buffer (2026-11-22) set the bound with rate.recode_overflow=1.0. The history run's CBR series starts with the 2026-11-09 build (CBR rate control first landed on 2026-11-07).
Timed like the main pages: the same bare-metal machines, at half load, with each day's build compiled for that machine. The machine selector switches between the x86 and Arm reports.

Every BD-J, ours and the references', is over the report's common set: the history clips on which every family of every day, at both key intervals, has well-formed curves. The 600-frame runs cover only the history subset's long clips, so the common set is those long clips; each clip counts once, its 150- and 600-frame windows averaged. The clip count is in each frame's heading.

Key interval: a key every 150 frames is the primary series; one key in 600 frames is the long-window view of key-frame and start-up behaviour (procedure section 14). The last build (the BP-4 benchmark build) was coded with one key in 600 frames only, so it is the last frame of that view alone.
References: the fixed builds of the same report, drawn as the same points on every frame, with their own front.
Compliance is each frame's worst over our families. AV2 key-frame positions are unchecked.
